output.question: If I decorate my Python function with @weave.op, will that alone give me the new Agents view with conversations and turns?
output.answer:
**No. `@weave.op` alone won't put your function in the Agents view.** Ops and agent tracing are separate workflows, and they record to different places.

- `weave.op` calls appear on the **Traces** page. Agent traces appear on the **Agents** page. You can use both in one project, but they produce separate traces [S1].
- Agent tracing uses the Weave SDK for Agents, which models conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool executions. Every turn, LLM call and tool call emits an OpenTelemetry span (a structured record of one operation). These spans are tagged with attributes such as `gen_ai.conversation.id` [S2].
- The Weave docs say that if you trace individual functions as Ops with `@weave.op`, you should follow the "Trace LLM applications" guide instead of the agent guide [S2].

**To get conversations and turns in the Agents view:**
1. Use a built-in integration. Install a plugin for your agent harness, or call `weave.init()` in code that uses a supported agent SDK. Weave then autopatches the framework and conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool calls show up in the Agents view [S3].
   - Harness plugins group turns into conversations on their own. With agent SDKs, your code decides which turns belong to the same conversation, so `weave.init()` alone isn't enough [S3].
2. Or, for a custom agent you build yourself, instrument it with the Weave SDK for Agents [S1, S2].

After that, open the **Agents** tab of your project to see the conversations [S2].

sources.heading: When to use agent tracing and when to use application instrumentation
sources.text:
### When to use agent tracing and when to use application instrumentation

Choose which workflow to use based on what you want to observe:

* **Use agent tracing if you're building or running an agent.** This is the right fit if you use a supported agent harness or agent SDK, or if you've built a custom agent that you can instrument yourself.

* **Use application instrumentation if you're tracing application code.** This is the right fit for applications structured around discrete calls rather than conversations, such as a RAG pipeline, a summarization endpoint, or custom business logic.

Each approach records traces in its own part of the UI: agent traces appear on the **Agents** page, and `weave.op` calls appear on the **Traces** page. You can use both approaches in the same Weave project, but they produce separate traces.

If you're not sure where to start and your system involves an agent, start with agent tracing using the [agent integration quickstart](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/agent-integration-quickstart.md). Otherwise, start with the [Op tracing quickstart](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/quickstart.md).

# What is Weave?

> Learn about W&B Weave and how it helps you build, evaluate, and improve LLM applications

W\&B Weave is an observability and evaluation platform for building reliable agents and LLM applications. Weave helps you understand what your AI application is doing, measure how well it performs, and systematically improve it over time.

Building LLM applications is fundamentally different from traditional software development. LLM outputs are non-deterministic, making debugging harder. Quality is subjective and context-dependent. Small prompt changes can cause unexpected behavior changes. Traditional testing approaches fall short.

sources.heading: Trace your agents
sources.text:
# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

sources.text:
# Choose an agent integration

> Pick a built-in Weave integration for your agent SDK or harness and start sending conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls to the Agents view.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/get-started/integrations.md).

W\&B Weave traces multi-turn agents built with popular SDKs and harnesses without hand-instrumenting each turn. Install a plugin for your agent harness, or call `weave.init()` in code that uses a supported agent SDK, and Weave autopatches the framework. Conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls render in the **Agents** view of your project.

Harness plugins group turns into conversations on their own, because the harness owns the session. Agent SDKs run one turn per call, so your code decides which turns belong to the same conversation. For those integrations, `weave.init()` alone isn't enough.

Choose from one of the following supported integrations.

results.title: Bedrock Agents
results.heading: Multi-turn conversations
results.snippet:
## Multi-turn conversations

Bedrock Agents preserve conversation state on the service side when you reuse a `sessionId`. To group multiple turns into a single trace in the Weights & Biases UI, wrap the turns in `weave.thread`:

```python lines theme={"system"}
with weave.thread("support-conversation") as t:
    for prompt in [
        "I can't log in to my account.",
        "I already tried resetting my password.",
    ]:
        ask_agent(prompt, session_id=t.thread_id)
```

Weave displays each turn in the UI as individual rows in the Threads view.

results.title: Trace your agents
results.heading: How data appears in the Weights & Biases UI
results.snippet:
## How data appears in the Weights & Biases UI

After you instrument your agent with the preceding patterns and run it, your traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project at `https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]/weave/agents`.

* The **Conversations tab** shows all conversations with a minimap of turn activity.
* The **Conversation detail view** opens when you click a conversation and shows all turns, its LLM calls, tool executions, token counts, and any attached feedback.

For details on viewing Agents data in Weave, see [View agent activity](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md).

## Get started

To open the Agents view for your project:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.
2. In the sidebar menu, select **Agents** to view all agent conversations saved for your project.

The Agents view is organized into a row of tabs across the top: **Dashboard**, **Agents**, **Conversations**, **Spans**, and **Signals**. The **Dashboard** tab gives a project-wide overview of agent activity, while the other tabs let you drill into individual agents, conversations, spans, and signals.

```python theme={"system"}
log_conversation(
```

### When to use agent tracing and when to use application instrumentation

Choose which workflow to use based on what you want to observe:

* **Use agent tracing if you're building or running an agent.** This is the right fit if you use a supported agent harness or agent SDK, or if you've built a custom agent that you can instrument yourself.

* **Use application instrumentation if you're tracing application code.** This is the right fit for applications structured around discrete calls rather than conversations, such as a RAG pipeline, a summarization endpoint, or custom business logic.

Each approach records traces in its own part of the UI: agent traces appear on the **Agents** page, and `weave.op` calls appear on the **Traces** page. You can use both approaches in the same Weave project, but they produce separate traces.

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

**No. `@weave.op` alone won't put your function in the Agents view.** Ops and agent tracing are separate workflows, and they record to different places.

- `weave.op` calls appear on the **Traces** page. Agent traces appear on the **Agents** page. You can use both in one project, but they produce separate traces [S1].
- The Agents view is built from agent tracing. It models conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool calls as OpenTelemetry spans (structured records of one operation). Each span carries attributes such as `gen_ai.conversation.id` [S2].
- The Weave docs say that if you trace individual functions as Ops with `@weave.op`, you should follow the "Trace LLM applications" guide instead of the agent guide [S2].

**To get conversations and turns in the Agents view:**
1. Use a built-in integration. Install a plugin for your agent harness, or call `weave.init()` in code that uses a supported agent SDK. Weave then autopatches the framework and conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool calls show up in the Agents view [S3].
2. Or, for a custom agent, instrument it yourself with the Weave agent tracing SDK. This means starting a conversation, then turns, LLM calls and tool calls [S2].

After that, open the **Agents** tab of your project to see the conversations [S2].
